scope.full_target:
# Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map

## Original exercise

Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.

> 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
> with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
> \[
> \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
>       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
> \]

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: n≥1 and m≥1 are integer dimensions.

binders.type: real scalar, existential at each point

hypotheses.statement: For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Delta u(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of any selected scalar is assumed.
For every pair of real times 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q whenever x∉C_[s,t] and r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. The energy E:(0,∞)→ℝ is differentiable and E'(t)=0 for every t>0; consequently E is constant on (0,∞). The energy is exactly ∫_{ℝ^n}(|u_t|²+|Du|²) dx with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.

correspondence.explanation: The parameters n,m are natural dimensions with H001 enforcing n,m≥1. Space d is standard real Euclidean d-space, with Fin d enumerating precisely the d original coordinates. H002 is joint C∞ regularity on the positive-time open set: ∞ in ℕ∞ω denotes all finite derivative orders and does not demand analyticity. The ambient total u represents the source positive-time map by restriction; conversely extend any source map arbitrarily (e.g. zero) on nonpositive times. All hypotheses and positive-time derivatives depend only on the restriction, so neither direction imposes an extension or boundary regularity assumption. H003 fixes a unit q; H004 is the original sphere condition. H005 is pointwise existence of a real scalar for the same normal acceleration, with no smooth scalar selection. H006 is the same compact support of u−q, locally uniform on each 0<s<t interval. Under smoothness, Fréchet derivatives on coordinate unit vectors and ordinary time derivatives give precisely the source component derivatives and Laplacian. volume is normalized Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and density is exactly ‖ut‖²+Σj‖uxj‖². The conclusion asserts integrability for every positive time, HasDerivAt energy 0 at every positive time, and equality of the energies at all positive time pairs. HasDerivAt is equivalent to differentiability together with derivative zero; the converse uses uniqueness of derivatives. Germ locality at t>0 makes this equivalent to the source energy on (0,∞), independent of the exterior representative. Thus the entire target, including all six hypotheses, time and spatial quantifiers, normalization and domain, is preserved in both directions. There are no E roots in the supplied source map.
